Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

rebelrebel 2026.11.12

  • A choice’s option may name a base map, base, shown while that value is the one chosen (by the list, by ‹ and ›, or in the address, unless the address names a base map of its own): a chart’s scale chosen with that chart beneath, so one control shows a scale’s features and its chart. All, several values, or a value with none leave the base map as it is.
  • Switching between two base maps written as styles with no glyphs did nothing: the page wrote glyphs: undefined into the new style, which fails MapLibre’s validation, and MapLibre then keeps the old style without a word. The glyphs are now left out where neither style has them.

rebelrebel 2026.11.11.4

  • A layer function sends a small layer whole by default: whole = NULL sends it to the page as one GeoJSON file when that is at most 5 MB (some 30,000 points), else as tiles; a table of more than 50,000 rows is not tried. Up to there the two were equal in a browser (fishycode’s whole-or-tiles study, 18 layers of real data), and a whole layer needs nothing more of R once read: a served map pans and zooms while R is busy. With R kept busy for 15 s, the survey’s points settled at a new view in 0.6-0.8 s whole, and in 14.5-14.6 s as tiles, once R was free. TRUE and FALSE still decide; another value is an error. The example data’s points, tows, paths and harbours now go whole; dansk’s 395,558 pings as tiles.
  • Once a map with a layer sent whole had been served, rr_stop(), and so a map served again on a port, stopped with “values must be length 1”: the layer’s table, which it has none of, was listed as NULL among the served maps’.

rebelrebel 2026.11.11.3

  • A bundle’s tiles are one file a layer: rr_bundle() writes a layer’s tiles, vector tiles and elevation images alike, as one PMTiles archive (version 3) in a script, tiles/<layer>.pmtiles.js, in place of a script for each tile, read in the page by the pmtiles library (4.5.0, BSD 3-Clause, in vendor/). A bundle is about a dozen files however many tiles it holds: dansk’s points to zoom 14, 13 files where there were 4,302; a 50 m grid’s elevation tiles to zoom 8, 12 where there were 623. Its tiles and their bytes are the same.
  • Opened from its folder, the page reads an archive whole: for 90-141 MB of tiles, a settled screen 1-2 s later and 300-650 MB more of Chrome’s memory than a file a tile took, and rr_bundle() says so of an archive over 100 MB. Put on a web host (http or https), the page reads only what the view needs, by range requests into the same file (base64 decodes from any multiple of four characters): as fast and as light as a file a tile, for 1.0-1.7 times its bytes. A host that answers no range sends the file whole, once.
  • A bundle’s base64 is decoded by the browser’s own Uint8Array.fromBase64() where it has one.

rebelrebel 2026.11.11.2

  • A map printed, or served by rr_serve() with no port, takes 8790 or, when another program holds it, the next free port to 8889: it stopped with “Port 8790 is taken: give another port” though no port had been given, as when another local service listened on 8790. Printed again, a map replaces the last one served with no port, where it is; a map on a port named is never replaced by one with no port. A port named and taken is still an error, and httpuv’s own line (“createTcpServer: address already in use”) is no longer printed before it. rr_serve(port = ) and rr_time(port = ) default to NULL; a layer function sets no port.

rebelrebel 2026.11.11.1

  • A bundle’s rows are read in a tenth of a second: rr_bundle() writes a layer’s rows as an array, row n at n - 1. Written as an object keyed by row number, dansk’s 395,558 rows (18-22 MB) took Chrome 65-71 s to read, so a bundle’s first click waited a minute for its row; and a row numbered 100,000, 200,000 or 300,000 was keyed as R prints it (1e+05), and a click on it found no row.
  • rr_bundle() writes a vector layer with no maxzoom to zoom 14, the page’s own deepest for its tiles, where the thinning stops too: the map of a layer function (rr_point() and the others) stopped with “its tiles’ deepest zoom is unknown”. Past it the map draws zoom 14’s tiles larger. dansk’s points to zoom 14 are 4,292 tiles and 90 MB; maxzoom = 12 writes 751 and 53 MB.
  • Checked: ramb’s maps article draws its points layer, coloured by behaviour or by speed with a legend for each and a click’s popup, in 55 lines of rb_map_layer(); rr_point(colour = c(behaviour, speed), popup = c(vessel_id, time_stamp, speed, behaviour)) draws it in five, its points also zoomed out (thinned) where the article’s needed minzoom = 10, served and as a bundle.

rebelrebel 2026.11.11

  • rr_tiles_dem() reads a grid where it is, through terra (now in Suggests) and GDAL: a GeoTIFF, a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF or any raster GDAL reads, in any projection; a terra SpatRaster; or, as before, a data frame of a grid’s cells (a lazy table of at most 10 million rows is read into R). Each tile is warped from the grid once: averaged where a pixel is wider than a cell, bilinear where it is narrower; a GeoTIFF’s overviews read only where a pixel spans eight cells or more (the file opened again with GDAL’s OVERVIEW_LEVEL=NONE for the rest, as terra hands the warp utility’s own -ovr no further). The DuckDB table of cells is gone. Measured on a 50 m grid of 523 million cells (287 million of them sea), each run a fresh R process: the first tile in under 2 s and 0.3-0.5 GB, where the table of cells took 23 s and 7 GB; every tile to zoom 8 in 80-86 s and 3 GB (1.7 GB from a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF), against 96 s and 8 GB; and the tiles three times closer to the grid at zoom 8 (0.07 m on average against 0.24 m), as the cells were a resampled copy.
  • Elevation tiles stop at zoom 8 by default (pixels of about 130 m at 65 degrees north), or at the grid’s own limit if it is coarser; maxzoom goes deeper.
  • A fit made in the page: a dem or contour layer on rr_tiles_dem()’s tiles fits its colours, contours and shading to the view from the tiles in view, served or in a bundle, with no call to R (by rr_bundle()’s default rules, which a served map’s config now carries). fit = TRUE asks the same of any elevation tiles; a function stays the server’s.
  • whole on rr_point(), rr_line(), rr_segment(), rr_polygon(), rr_text() and rr_path(): TRUE sends a layer’s rows to the page as one GeoJSON file, read once by MapLibre’s worker; by default, as before, as tiles.
  • A tile holds the features within its margin (64 of its 4,096 units past each edge): a point just past a tile’s edge was in neither tile’s drawing, and vanished.
  • A bundle opened from its folder: a tile it does not hold is empty, not an error (points were drawn twice where a tile was missing), and a layer’s rows are read once, not at each click.
  • A bundle’s contours reach the grid’s edge: an elevation tile it does not hold, beyond the grid or not written, is level at nodata, as a served map’s is. maplibre-contour draws no lines in a tile with a neighbour refused, and on a small grid most of a view went without (6 line pieces where the served map drew 74).

rebelrebel 2026.11.10.8

  • An id is a list, not a range: in choose, a whole number (stored as an integer) is a list, as text is, and a fraction, a date or a time a range. Where the data’s dictionary (data-dict.tidyverse.org’s, in the parquet file’s metadata) gives a column’s type, it decides: number(id), enum, string or boolean a list, number, number(quantity), date or datetime a range. A number declared an id is coloured as categories too, and written whole (1131, not 1131.0).
  • The examples’ ids are stored as integers: trawlsurvey‘s vid and trawlsurveytows’ id.lgs, every row and the files’ metadata kept (data-raw/integer_ids.R).
  • rr_map("file.parquet") reads the file: a path given to the map itself was not read before.
  • A dictionary’s YAML keeps n, y, no, yes, on and off as written: a column called n stopped the reader.

rebelrebel 2026.11.10.7

  • choose takes ranges: a number, a date or a time is a slider with two handles, over each of its values where it has at most 64 (years, days), else over bins between pretty() breaks; text, a factor or a logical stays a list, as colour reads them. Ranges and lists are linked by the same counts (a vessel chosen, the days’ range spans its days), ‹ and › step one value at a time over the values with rows or move the window by its width, and the address holds day=2019-03-01..2019-03-03. A numeric id is a list once it is text: as.character(as.integer(id)).
  • A path is split by a range’s bins, so a range chosen shows whole runs of it; the view fits the combinations every choice leaves, and stays where it is when a range is slid.

rebelrebel 2026.11.10.6

  • Points are thinned in each tile by default (rr_point(thin = TRUE)): one a screen pixel, each colour (a number’s in eight classes), each value a choose list picks and each group of a time panel keeping its own, so a tile of millions of rows reaches the page as what can be seen of it. From the layer’s deepest zoom (maxzoom, 14 by default) only points that would be drawn on one spot are dropped, so every point that can be told apart can be clicked. On a year of national AIS pings (32.8 million), the busiest tile at zoom 6 went from 245 MB and 8.9 s to 8.7 MB and 0.9 s; at zoom 14, from 51 MB to 3.9 MB. thin = FALSE keeps every point; a number of pixels thins more.
  • A point’s size follows the zoom by default: 2 pixels across until the zoom at which most points lie that far apart, then doubling with each zoom in, as a size on the ground does, up to 8. size = c(1, 12) sets other bounds, one number a size that stays. The outline shows once a point is 3 pixels across.
  • rr_tiles_table(thin = ), the same for any table of points; a thinned tile’s features in the table’s order, so its bytes are the same every time.

rebelrebel 2026.11.10.5

  • choose on a layer function is that layer’s own: its lists under its name in the sidebar, over it alone, linked as the map’s are, and in the page’s address under the layer’s id and the field (pings_vid=1131). A path is split by its own choose columns too, so a choice shows whole lines. Before, a layer function that started a map gave its choose to the map; the map’s lists are now given to rr_map() alone.
  • Lists over shapes (rr_line(), rr_polygon()) take each value’s extent from its shapes.

rebelrebel 2026.11.10.4

  • choose‘s lists are linked: each offers only the values the other lists’ choices leave, from the combinations the data hold, with their rows counted again; a choice the others no longer leave goes back to all, the last list first (a trip gives way to its vessel), and ‹ and › step through the values left. So choose = c(vid, tid) needs no nesting declared: a vessel chosen leaves its trips.

rebelrebel 2026.11.10.3

  • A click shows the feature’s row as a table: the tiles carry the row’s number and title only, and the server answers /row/<layer>/<n> with the columns popup names (2-3 ms a click); a bundle writes a layer’s rows beside its tiles, up to 2 million values. Whole numbers as they are, fractions to six significant digits in the page’s language, yes and no, a dash where missing; a web address a link, a picture’s address the picture, a video’s a link.
  • labels and codes in every layer function: a column’s name, unit and description, and a coded column’s labels, by default from the data (a data frame’s label and units attributes, or a parquet file’s own dictionary in data-dict.tidyverse.org’s format).
  • rr_path() takes a number as its order (a sequence, a distance along a transect) as well as a time.

rebelrebel 2026.11.10.2

  • The layer functions, built with the pipe: rr_point(), rr_path() (rows joined in time, a line per group, one column or several), rr_line(), rr_segment() (a line from each row’s start to its end), rr_polygon() and rr_text(), one internal function for all. They take their arguments in one order and words (colour, fill, size, linewidth, opacity, label; palette, limits, stretch, legend; popup, hover, choose; name, info, section, visible; minzoom, maxzoom). A bare name is a column, a string a value.
  • rr_map(data) starts a map the layer functions add to; choose names the columns the reader picks, sections the sidebar’s boxes. A layer function given data first starts a map. Data are a parquet file, folder or glob, a lazy DuckDB table, a data frame or an sf object.
  • Colours from the data: Okabe-Ito for up to eight values, Paired for up to twelve, Glasbey’s 32 beyond, the rest grey as “other”; viridis for ordered factors, numbers, dates and times (over the 1st to 99th percentile, or limits, stretched linearly, on a log scale or in equal shares). palette overrides them: a name written loosely, colours, colours by value, or a function of n.
  • The time panel is generic: rr_time() takes its columns (col, no default) and its group (by) from the call or from the map (a path’s group and time); interval tables are read by start and end, or as named; the page names the group’s list by its column and counts rows. Points carry their time and group for it.
  • The quick look at vessels’ pings and tracks is no longer here: it is ramb’s, as wrappers over these functions.

rebelrebel 2026.11.10.1

  • The base maps are those that show the sea floor: EMODnet’s sea floor (its 2020 base layer), the first and the one a map opens on; the same darkened (emodnet_dark); EMODnet’s lighter atlas (v12); and Esri’s ocean, which reaches beyond Europe’s seas; and none. Carto’s Positron, Voyager and Dark Matter (a flat sea) and Esri’s satellite tiles are no longer offered. Each picture has a Carto style’s place and sea names drawn over it (Positron’s, or Dark Matter’s on the dark one), which also give the layers’ own labels their fonts: a base map’s labels, label_layers, paint and background in rr_basemaps(). The page opens on a picture base map.

rebelrebel 2026.11.10

  • The package starts as ramb’s map viewer, moved here unchanged but for its names: rb_map() is rr_map(), rb_map_layer() rr_layer(), rb_map_group() rr_section(), rb_map_serve() and rb_map_stop() rr_serve() and rr_stop(), rb_map_bundle() rr_bundle(), the tile makers rr_tiles_table(), rr_tiles_dem() and rr_tiles_mbtiles(), rr_palettes(), rr_basemaps(), rr_notes(), rr_notes_add(), rr_verdicts() and rr_time(); ramb’s rb_read_example() is rr_example(), with five of ramb’s datasets (dansk, dansk_harbours, dansk_relief, trawlsurvey, trawlsurveytows). rb_map_pings() and rb_map_track() are internal until rr_point() and rr_path() take their place.
  • The page’s libraries are in the package (inst/engine/vendor): MapLibre GL JS 5.24.0, maplibre-contour 0.1.1 and uPlot 1.6.30, served by rr_serve() at /vendor/ and copied into a bundle’s vendor folder, so a map draws with no network but the base map’s.
